title: IMPULSA IGUALDAD Welcomes Disability Law Reform, Calls for Reinstatement of Vetted Measures
summary: The Spanish disability federation IMPULSA IGUALDAD praised the final approval of reforms to the General Law on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and the Personal Autonomy and Dependence Care Law. The reforms strengthen rights, promote independent living, and consolidate universal accessibility. However, the organization urges the government to recover amendments vetoed during legislative proceedings, including reduced VAT for architectural barrier removal, specific tax benefits for dependent individuals, and improved financing for the care system.
body:
The Spanish disability federation IMPULSA IGUALDAD praised the final approval of reforms to the General Law on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and the Personal Autonomy and Dependence Care Law. The reforms strengthen rights, promote independent living, and consolidate universal accessibility. However, the organization urges the government to recover amendments vetoed during legislative proceedings, including reduced VAT for architectural barrier removal, specific tax benefits for dependent individuals, and improved financing for the care system.

title: France: 21 Years After the 2005 Law, Final Decrees on Disability Accessibility Published
summary: More than twenty years after the adoption of the 2005 disability law, new decrees were published on September 2 and 3 to clarify pending provisions. The measures aim to improve the reception of deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals in public services and enhance the accessibility of professional buildings. The article discusses the reasons for the significant delay in finalizing these regulations.

title: ONCE Launches Accessible Edition of 'Leo XIV, the Lion of Peace' for Visually Impaired Readers
summary: The Spanish National Organization of the Blind (ONCE) has released an accessible version of the book 'Leo XIV, the Lion of Peace' to coincide with Pope Leo XIV's 71st birthday. The edition is available in audio, Braille, and large print formats through the ONCE Digital Library, which serves over 72,000 members. The text highlights the bridge-building nature of the Pope's leadership and his recent interactions with students and individuals with disabilities in Spain, emphasizing inclusive access to culture.
body:
The Spanish National Organization of the Blind (ONCE) has released an accessible version of the book 'Leo XIV, the Lion of Peace' to coincide with Pope Leo XIV's 71st birthday. The edition is available in audio, Braille, and large print formats through the ONCE Digital Library, which serves over 72,000 members. The text highlights the bridge-building nature of the Pope's leadership and his recent interactions with students and individuals with disabilities in Spain, emphasizing inclusive access to culture.
